chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said:

If the earth is wet and there is no dust nor water in it, look for the driest place you can find and perform Tayammum from its dust or something covered in dust; and if it is a situation where you can find nothing except clay, then there is no problem if you were to perform Tayammum with it.
ai.seo_question: How to perform Tayammum when the ground is wet and there is no dry dust?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the practical application of Tayammum by prioritizing the driest available earth when moisture is present, ensuring the validity of the ritual when water is scarce. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir) in times of travel or necessity, allowing the use of clay if no dust is found, thereby preventing hardship in purification. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law in adapting ritual purity requirements to varying environmental conditions.
